coverage_notes: This exhaustive survey covers six major angles: (1) Foundational XAI theory and surveys—meta-analyses and systematic reviews from peer-reviewed venues (T0), including comprehensive XAI taxonomies and surveys spanning methods, challenges, and evaluation. (2) Trust in AI systems from HCI perspective—peer-reviewed literature on how explainability affects user trust calibration, with frameworks distinguishing technical, design, and socio-ethical factors. (3) Canonical methodologies—landmark papers on LIME, SHAP, anchors, TCAV, Grad-CAM, and LRP that operationalize explanation; plus foundational cognitive science work on what constitutes good explanations (contrastive, selective, causal). (4) Model documentation standards—model cards, datasheets, and transparency artifacts emerging from Gebru/Mitchell et al. as regulatory and best-practice baselines. (5) RAG-specific transparency and evaluation—source attribution, retrieval grounding, and trustworthiness in retrieval-augmented systems, directly addressing the corpus's RAG-UX wedge. (6) High-stakes domain applications—healthcare, criminal justice, finance—showing explainability's role in trust and accountability, plus GDPR/regulatory context. Secondary angles include mechanistic interpretability for AI safety, uncertainty quantification, explanation robustness, human-AI collaboration, and cognitive load in explanation design. Seminal authors captured: Tufte (visualization), Norman/Shneiderman (HCI), Rudin (interpretable ML), Pirolli (information foraging), Caruana (medical intelligibility), Lipton (calibration). Coverage spans T0 meta-analyses and systematic reviews; T1 peer-reviewed methods papers from ACM CHI/UIST/TOCHI, FAccT, AIES, EMNLP, and arXiv; T2 textbooks and foundational practitioner essays from classical HCI and data visualization. Notable gaps: limited coverage of explanation-user-performance causality studies (few show improvements), edge cases in LLM transparency beyond mechanistic MI, and interactive/iterative explanation systems in production. ~32 sources across 4 tiers.

sources.title: Explainable AI (XAI): A Systematic Meta-Survey of Current Challenges and Future Opportunities
sources.notes: Meta-survey organizing challenges and research directions in XAI; foundational reference for field scope and taxonomy.

sources.title: A Systematic Literature Review of User Trust in AI-Enabled Systems: An HCI Perspective
sources.notes: Systematic review mapping trust in AI from HCI lens; identifies socio-ethical, technical, and design factors influencing trust.

sources.title: Trust in Human-AI Interaction: Scoping Out Models, Measures, and Methods
sources.notes: Scoping review of trust models and measurement methods in human-AI interaction; establishes conceptual foundations.

sources.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
sources.notes: Foundational paper (Gebru et al.) establishing model cards as standardized documentation for AI transparency and accountability.

sources.title: What's documented in AI? Systematic Analysis of 32K AI Model Cards
sources.notes: Empirical analysis of model card adoption and documentation quality across 32K cards; shows state of transparency practice.

sources.title: LIME: Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations
sources.notes: Seminal Ribeiro et al. paper introducing LIME; canonical model-agnostic local explanation method widely used in practice.

sources.title: Anchors: High-Precision Model-Agnostic Explanations
sources.notes: Ribeiro et al. on rule-based local explanations with high-precision guarantees; foundational for rule extraction methods.

sources.title: SHAP - Interpretable Machine Learning
sources.notes: Comprehensive reference on SHAP (Lundberg & Lee); game-theoretic approach to feature attribution now standard in industry.

sources.title: Interpretable Machine Learning: Fundamental Principles and 10 Grand Challenges
sources.notes: Rudin's foundational essay on interpretability principles and open challenges; shapes discourse on interpretable-by-design models.

sources.title: Intelligible Models for HealthCare: Predicting Pneumonia Risk and Hospital 30-day Readmission
sources.notes: Caruana et al. landmark paper showing high-accuracy interpretable models in medical domain; central to accuracy-interpretability tradeoff debate.

sources.title: European Union Regulations on Algorithmic Decision-Making and a 'Right to Explanation'
sources.notes: Foundational legal analysis of GDPR and algorithmic transparency requirements; establishes regulatory context for explainability.

sources.title: Alterfactual Explanations -- The Relevance of Irrelevance for Explaining AI Systems
sources.notes: Theoretical framework on contrastive and counterfactual explanations; connects to cognitive science of explanation.

sources.title: What makes a good explanation? Cognitive Dimensions of Explaining Intelligent Machines
sources.notes: Tim Miller et al.; foundational cognitive science framework on explanation properties (contrastive, selective, causal).

sources.title: The Mythos of Model Interpretability
sources.notes: Lipton's influential critique of interpretability as nebulous concept; establishes need for grounded, application-specific definitions.

sources.title: Enforcing Interpretability and its Statistical Impacts: Trade-offs Between Accuracy and Interpretability
sources.notes: Empirical study questioning the necessity of accuracy-interpretability tradeoff; challenges common assumptions.

sources.title: It's Complicated: The Relationship between User Trust, Model Accuracy and Explanations in AI
sources.notes: ACM TOCHI empirical study on how explanations and accuracy jointly influence user trust calibration.

sources.title: Evaluating Explainable AI: Which Algorithmic Explanations Help Users Predict Model Behavior?
sources.notes: Empirical evaluation of whether explanations actually help users predict model behavior; addresses explanation utility.

sources.title: How Human-Centered Explainable AI Interface Are Designed and Evaluated: A Systematic Survey
sources.notes: Systematic survey of XUI design and evaluation methods; bridges XAI and HCI interface design.

sources.title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
sources.notes: Survey of RAG trustworthiness factors including retrieval transparency and source attribution; directly addresses corpus wedge.

sources.title: Trust Me on This: A User Study of Trustworthiness for RAG Responses
sources.notes: Empirical user study on factors affecting trust in RAG-generated responses; shows importance of source transparency.

sources.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Large Language Model Alignment: Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions
sources.notes: Comprehensive review of mechanistic interpretability for LLM alignment; establishes connection to AI safety.

sources.title: TCAV: Relative Concept Importance Testing with Linear Concept Activation Vectors
sources.notes: Been Kim et al.; foundational concept-based explanation method for neural networks.

sources.title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
sources.notes: Selvaraju et al.; widely-used method for CNN visual explanation; applicable across model architectures.

sources.title: Layer-wise Relevance Propagation for Deep Neural Network Architectures
sources.notes: Montavon & Samek; principled approach to decomposing neural network decisions via backpropagation of relevance.

sources.title: A Comprehensive Study on Fidelity Metrics for XAI
sources.notes: Comprehensive benchmark of faithfulness/fidelity metrics for explanation quality; addresses evaluation challenges.

sources.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Confidence Calibration in Large Language Models: A Survey
sources.notes: 2025 survey on uncertainty and calibration in LLMs; critical for trustworthy explanations.

sources.title: Toward a Science of Human-AI Teaming for Decision Making: A Complementarity Framework
sources.notes: Integrative framework for human-AI collaborative decision-making and complementarity.

sources.title: Explainable AI in Healthcare: A Systematic Review of XAI Use Cases in Imaging, Diagnostics, and Rehabilitation
sources.notes: Domain-specific systematic review of XAI in healthcare; shows application priorities and method effectiveness.

sources.title: A Survey on Bias and Fairness in Machine Learning
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey connecting bias, fairness, and interpretability; essential for responsible AI context.

sources.title: The Purpose of Visualization is Insight, Not Pictures: An Interview with Ben Shneiderman
sources.notes: Shneiderman's foundational principles on information visualization for analytical reasoning; establishes design philosophy.

sources.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
sources.notes: Tufte's seminal work on data visualization principles; establishes aesthetic and cognitive foundations for explanation design.

sources.title: The Design of Everyday Things (Revised Edition)
sources.notes: Don Norman's foundational HCI work on mental models, affordances, and user-centered design; frames explanation as design problem.

sources.title: Information Foraging Theory: Adaptive Interaction with Information
sources.notes: Pirolli's ecological theory of information seeking and sensemaking; informs explanation interface design for cognitive efficiency.

sources.title: A Comprehensive Taxonomy for Explainable Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Survey of Surveys on Methods and Concepts
sources.notes: Meta-taxonomy synthesizing 50+ XAI surveys; authoritative reference for method classification and field organization.

sources.title: Establishing and Evaluating Trustworthy AI: Overview and Research Challenges
sources.notes: Comprehensive framework for trustworthy AI with evaluation criteria; synthesizes explainability within broader trust context.
